issues.claim: Hence a reasonable guideline: a service is no larger than a context and no smaller than an aggregate, and non-functional requirements decide everything between these bounds.
issues.problem: The "no larger than a context" half is supported by the cited Microsoft excerpt ("shouldn't span more than one bounded context"). The "no smaller than an aggregate" lower bound is not shown in the excerpt, which only says aggregates are "often good candidates" for microservices. The generator itself says it did not verify the page and wording. The lower bound is also stated flatly in answer point 4 ("Never split an aggregate across services") without a source.
issues.suggestedFix: Add the Microsoft tactical-DDD page https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/microservices/model/tactical-ddd (lang en, kind docs) with linkTitles in ru and en, and cite it for the lower bound. Or soften the claim to "aggregates are often good candidates for services, so splitting below an aggregate usually breaks invariants". Apply the same change in locales.ru.

issues.claim: The cost of a mistake is asymmetric: merging services that are too small back together is usually harder than carving a part out of a larger one, so start with the coarser cut.
issues.problem: This is the generator's experience-based judgement. Neither cited page states it, and the Microsoft excerpt says non-functional factors can push toward either splitting or merging. A candidate could learn it as sourced fact.
issues.suggestedFix: Phrase it as practitioner opinion, e.g. "in practice it is often easier to carve a part out of a larger service than to merge many chatty ones back". Or drop "usually" and the asymmetry claim and keep only "start coarser and split when a measured reason appears". Mirror the change in locales.ru.

issues.claim: 3. ... a different release cadence, fault isolation ... (point 5)
issues.problem: The Microsoft excerpt lists team size, data types, technologies, scalability, availability and security. Release cadence and fault isolation are a reasonable synthesis but are not on the page.
issues.suggestedFix: Keep them, but attribute them to the "availability and deployment requirements" family, or leave as is since they are defensible.

issues.claim: The alternative is a database (or at least a private schema) per service, with access to another service's data only through the owner's API or through integration events
issues.problem: The cited pages support a private data store per service. The data sovereignty page says "Each BC must have its own model and database". The excerpts do not support "or at least a private schema", and this softens the cited guidance. The generator flagged the same doubt.
issues.suggestedFix: Write "a database per service (some teams accept private tables or a private schema per service with enforced access rules as a weaker variant, but separate databases give real isolation)". Or remove the parenthetical. Mirror the change in locales.ru ("база (или хотя бы закрытая схема) на сервис").
